Each SERCOM is one serial engine that is set up as an I2C (SMBus-compatible), SPI or USART interface; once enabled in a mode, all of its resources serve that mode. It holds a transmitter with a single buffer, a receiver with a two-level buffer, a baud-rate generator and address match and mask logic. It runs from its generic clock or an external clock, works in every sleep mode and can be served by DMA. Its signals leave through four internal pads, PAD[3:0], which a multiplexer assigns per mode.

The bus clock CLK_SERCOMx_APB is on at reset and is switched in the Power Manager. Two generic clocks feed the SERCOM: GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE, needed to run as a master, and GCLK_SERCOMx_SLOW, needed only by some functions; both are set up in GCLK before use. They are asynchronous to the bus clock, so some register writes are synchronized. Pins are assigned through PORT. The SERCOM has DMA request lines and one interrupt line and no events. It keeps running when the CPU is halted by a debugger unless set to halt.
The PAC can write-protect every writable register except INTFLAG, ADDR and DATA. Write protection is lifted while the CPU is halted in debug mode.

Transmit side: one write buffer feeding a shift register. Receive side: a shift register feeding a two-level buffer. The baud generator runs from GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE or an external clock. Address matching serves SPI and I2C.
CTRLA.MODE picks the mode. CTRLA.ENABLE = 1 enables the SERCOM and 0 disables it. CTRLA.SWRST = 1 resets every register except DBGCTRL and leaves the SERCOM disabled.

The generator divides the baud reference clock fREF (the serial engine clock, internal or external) by the BAUD value. Asynchronous mode transmits on the divide-by-16 output and receives on the divide-by-1 output; synchronous mode uses divide-by-2. The choice follows the operating mode. Asynchronous arithmetic mode uses a 16-bit BAUD (0 to 65,535); asynchronous fractional mode a 13-bit BAUD of at least 1 and a 3-bit fraction; synchronous mode an 8-bit BAUD (0 to 255).

Address matching works on seven or eight bits and has three forms. Address with mask: ADDR.ADDR matches with the bits set in ADDR.ADDRMASK ignored, so an all-zero mask matches one address and an all-ones mask accepts every address. Two unique addresses: ADDR.ADDR and ADDR.ADDRMASK each match. Range: every address from ADDR.ADDRMASK (lower limit) to ADDR.ADDR (upper limit) inclusive matches.

Interrupt sources depend on the mode. Each has a flag in INTFLAG, enabled through INTENSET and disabled through INTENCLR; a request stays active until the flag is cleared, the interrupt disabled or the SERCOM reset. All sources share one interrupt line. The SERCOM runs in any sleep mode in which its serial clock (external or from the baud-rate generator) runs, and its interrupts wake the device.

Registers that cross from the bus clock CLK_SERCOMx_APB to the core clock GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE set STATUS.SYNCBUSY at once and clear it when done; the Synchronization Ready interrupt can signal the end. Another synchronized access while SYNCBUSY is set stalls the bus (and the CPU, with interrupts pending) until it completes.

USART is a SERCOM mode. Features: full duplex; asynchronous with clock recovery, or synchronous; internal or external clock in both; 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9 data bits and 1 or 2 stop bits; odd or even parity; LSB or MSB first; overflow and frame error detection; noise filtering with false start-bit rejection and a digital low-pass filter; collision detection; operation in every sleep mode; up to half the system clock on an internal clock and up to the system clock on an external one; RTS/CTS flow control; IrDA up to 115.2 kbps; LIN slave with auto-baud and break detection; start-of-frame detection; DMA. The write buffer lets frames follow each other with no gap.

The USART keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock runs, and its interrupts wake the device. It needs GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE set up in GCLK; CLK_SERCOMx_APB is switched in the PM. The PAC can protect every writable register except INTFLAG, STATUS and DATA; protection is lifted while the CPU is halted in debug and never applies to an external debugger. It has DMA requests and an interrupt line, and no events. DBGCTRL can halt it while the CPU is halted.

Lines: RxD receives, TxD transmits, XCK carries the clock in synchronous mode. A frame is a start bit (low), 5 to 9 data bits LSB or MSB first, an optional even or odd parity bit after the data, and 1 or 2 stop bits (high). A frame may follow straight on, or the line idles high.

CTRLA (but ENABLE and SWRST), CTRLB (but RXEN and TXEN) and BAUD are writable only while the USART is disabled; writes while it is enabled or enabling are dropped, and writes while it is disabling land once it is off. Setup order: CTRLA.MODE = 0x0 (external clock) or 0x1 (internal clock); CTRLA.CMODE for asynchronous or synchronous; CTRLA.RXPO for the receive pad; CTRLA.TXPO for the transmit and clock pads; CTRLB.CHSIZE; CTRLA.DORD; for parity CTRLB.PMODE and CTRLA.FORM = 0x1; CTRLB.SBMODE for stop bits; BAUD when on the internal clock; then CTRLB.RXEN and CTRLB.TXEN.
CTRLA.ENABLE = 1 enables and 0 disables. CTRLA.SWRST = 1 resets every register except DBGCTRL and disables the USART.

CTRLA.CMODE = 1 selects synchronous mode and 0 asynchronous. CTRLA.MODE = 0x1 takes the clock from the baud-rate generator; 0x0 takes it from XCK. Asynchronous mode uses the 16-bit BAUD; synchronous mode uses its eight LSBs.

In synchronous mode CTRLA.MODE decides whether XCK is an output or an input. RxD is sampled on the opposite XCK edge to the one that changes TxD. CTRLA.CPOL = 0: data changes on the rising edge and is sampled on the falling edge; CTRLA.CPOL = 1: changes on the falling edge, sampled on the rising edge. With the clock on XCK (MODE = 0x0) the shift registers run straight from XCK, unsynchronized to the system clock, so XCK may run up to the system frequency.

Transmit and receive data share the DATA address: a write fills TxDATA, a read returns RxDATA. Writing DATA starts a transmission; the character moves to the shift register when it is empty and a whole frame goes out. INTFLAG.DRE says DATA may be written. INTFLAG.TXC sets when a frame and its stop bits are out and DATA holds nothing new. Clearing CTRLB.TXEN takes effect only once the shift register and TxDATA are empty.

Reception begins on a valid start bit; bits are sampled at the baud rate or on XCK until the first stop bit, then the frame moves into the two-level receive buffer and INTFLAG.RXC sets. A second stop bit is ignored. DATA is read only after RXC. Clearing CTRLB.RXEN flushes the buffer and loses a reception in progress. STATUS holds FERR, BUFOVF and PERR, each set until written with one and cleared when the receiver is disabled. With CTRLA.IBON = 1 BUFOVF sets at the moment of overflow; with 0 it travels with the data and sets alongside RXC when that data is read.

A clock recovery unit locks incoming frames to the internal baud clock and a data recovery unit samples and low-pass filters each bit. How far the incoming rate may stray is set by how exact the internal baud clock is, by the incoming rate and by the frame length; reference clock instability and the generator's inexact division both add error, so BAUD is chosen for the least error.
CTRLA.FORM = 0x1 enables parity. CTRLB.PMODE = 0 gives even parity (the parity bit makes the count of ones even) and 1 odd. On reception a mismatch sets STATUS.PERR.

RTS and CTS connect crosswise to the remote device's CTS and RTS. Handshaking needs the internal clock (CTRLA.MODE = 1), asynchronous mode (CTRLA.CMODE = 0) and CTRLA.TXPO = 2, the pinout with flow control. RTS is driven high while it is disabled or its FIFO is full, telling the remote to stop after the current frame; toggling RXEN moves RTS after a synchronization delay; on a full FIFO RTS rises at once and the frame being received waits in the shift register. STATUS.CTS shows the CTS level; a character starts only while CTS is low, and when CTS rises the transmitter stops after the current frame.

IrDA-compliant up to 115.2 kb/s with CTRLB.ENC = 1, asynchronous mode (CTRLA.CMODE = 0) and 16x sampling (CTRLA.SAMPR[0] = 0). Each low bit is sent as a high pulse 3/16 of a bit period wide. The decoder resynchronizes on each zero pulse and accepts a pulse that meets the minimum width set in RXPL.RXPL, passing it to the receiver at mid-bit. For example RXPL.RXPL = 19 needs 20 SE clocks, which with BAUD = 0xE666 (160 SE clocks a bit) is 2/16 of a bit. Transmit and receive polarities are opposite: a zero goes out as a high pulse and an accepted pulse is read as a zero.

Available with CTRLA.FORM = 0x04 or 0x05, asynchronous mode and 16x fractional sampling (CTRLA.SAMPR = 1), in LIN format. More than 11 consecutive dominant bits at the set baud rate are a break: INTFLAG.RXBRK sets and the next character is expected to be the 0x55 sync. A counter runs over the 8 bit times of the sync field; its top 13 bits (count divided by 8) become BAUD.BAUD and its low 3 bits BAUD.FP, loaded after a synchronization delay. A sync character other than 0x55 sets STATUS.ISF and INTFLAG.ERROR and leaves the baud rate alone. Data characters follow the sync field.

With transmitter and receiver joined, by pin setup or outside, CTRLB.COLDEN = 1 (with RXEN and TXEN both 1) compares each received bit with the bit sent. Receiving while the transmitter is idle is no collision. On a collision the transfer aborts, the transmit buffer is flushed, the transmitter disables (CTRLB.TXEN = 0, SYNCBUSY.CTRLB set until done) and TxD goes tri-state, STATUS.COLL and INTFLAG.ERROR set, and INTFLAG.TXC sets as the buffer is empty. Software re-enables the transmitter once SYNCBUSY.CTRLB is clear.
Setting CTRLA.RXPO and CTRLA.TXPO to the same pad loops transmit to receive through the pad, so the signal also appears on the pin.

CTRLB.SFDE = 1 lets a start bit wake the CPU, in asynchronous and synchronous modes. In standby the 8MHz internal oscillator must clock GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE: a falling edge on RxD powers it up and enables the USART clock, and the frame is received if the baud rate is slow against the oscillator's start-up time, which varies with supply and temperature. With INTENSET.RXS set the Receive Start interrupt fires on the start bit; without it the oscillator and USART clock stay on through the frame and the CPU wakes on Receive Complete, if enabled.
In asynchronous mode the bit value is a majority vote of three middle samples chosen by CTRLA.SAMPA. With SAMPA = 0 they are samples 7, 8 and 9 at 16x oversampling and 3, 4 and 5 at 8x.

DMA: RX is requested while the receive FIFO holds data and cleared by reading DATA; TX is requested while TX DATA is empty and cleared by writing DATA. Interrupts: Error, Received Break, Clear to Send Input Change, Receive Start, Receive Complete, Transmit Complete and Data Register Empty, on one shared line, each with a flag in INTFLAG enabled by INTENSET and disabled by INTENCLR. No events.

Internal clock: CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1 keeps GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE running in every sleep mode and any interrupt wakes the device. External clock: RUNSTDBY = 1 lets Receive Start or Receive Complete wake it. With RUNSTDBY = 0 the internal clock stops when the current transfer ends and Receive Start or Transfer Complete can wake the device; an external clock is disconnected when the current transfer ends and further reception is dropped.

Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLB.RXEN and CTRLB.TXEN are synchronized; SYNCBUSY.SWRST, SYNCBUSY.ENABLE and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB are set while each is in progress. A synchronized access while its SYNCBUSY bit is set gives a peripheral bus error.

SPI is a SERCOM mode: full duplex over four wires (SCK, MOSI, MISO and SS), with a single-buffered transmitter and a double-buffered receiver, all four SPI modes, single-direction operation that frees MISO or MOSI, LSB or MSB first, and DMA. As master it runs SCK up to 12MHz from an 8-bit clock generator and can drive SS in hardware. As slave it takes SCK up to the system clock, offers 8-bit address matching, works in every sleep mode and wakes on an SS transition.

In master mode SS is driven by hardware when CTRLB.MSSEN = 1. The SPI keeps running in any sleep mode and its interrupts wake the device. It needs GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE set up in GCLK; CLK_SERCOMx_APB is switched in the PM. It has DMA requests and an interrupt line, and no events. The PAC can protect every writable register except INTFLAG, STATUS and DATA; protection is lifted while the CPU is halted in debug and never applies to an external debugger. DBGCTRL can halt it while the CPU is halted.

The master starts and controls every transaction; the slave answers. While a character shifts, the next can be loaded into DATA; each received character moves into the two-level receive buffer. A transaction is one or more 8- or 9-bit characters. The master pulls the slave's SS low, generates SCK, shifts out on MOSI while the slave shifts out on MISO, one character in for each character out, and ends the transaction by raising SS.

CTRLA (but ENABLE and SWRST), CTRLB (but RXEN), BAUD and ADDR are writable only while the SPI is disabled; writes while it is enabled or enabling are dropped and writes while disabling land once it is off. Setup: CTRLA.MODE = 0x2 (slave) or 0x3 (master); CTRLA.CPOL and CTRLA.CPHA; CTRLA.FORM; CTRLA.DIPO for the receive pad; CTRLA.DOPO for the transmit, SS and SCK pads; CTRLB.CHSIZE; CTRLA.DORD; BAUD for a master; CTRLB.MSSEN = 1 for hardware SS on a master; then CTRLB.RXEN. CTRLA.ENABLE enables, CTRLA.SWRST resets every register but DBGCTRL and disables the SPI.

As master (MODE = 0x3) SCK comes from the baud-rate generator in synchronous mode using the 8-bit BAUD. As slave (MODE = 0x2) the master's SCK clocks the shift register directly. TxDATA and RxDATA share the DATA address: a write fills TxDATA, a read returns RxDATA.

With CTRLB.MSSEN = 0 SS can be any GPIO set as an output, driven low by software before a transaction and high after; with MSSEN = 1 hardware drives it. A character written to DATA moves to the shift register when it is empty, which sets INTFLAG.DRE so the next can be written. With the receiver enabled each received character moves into the receive buffer on the clock of its last bit and sets INTFLAG.RXC. INTFLAG.TXC sets when the last character is out and DATA is empty.

While SS is high the slave is idle and MISO tri-state; DATA may be written whenever INTFLAG.DRE is set. With SS low and SCK running it samples and shifts by the set mode; DRE sets when TxDATA is loaded into the shift register, and each received character moves into the receive buffer on its last bit and sets RXC. Raising SS ends the transaction and sets TXC. A write to DATA needs up to three SCK cycles before it can be loaded, and is loaded at the next character boundary, so the first character of a transaction is not DATA unless preloaded. Within a transaction the next character must be written with at least three SCK cycles of the current one left, or the last received character goes out again. INTFLAG.DRE sets three CLK_SERCOM_APB cycles after DATA empties.

STATUS.BUFOVF is the one error bit; it stays set until written with one and clears when the receiver is disabled. With CTRLA.IBON = 1 it sets at the moment of overflow and software empties the FIFO by reading until INTFLAG.RXC clears. With IBON = 0 the overflow travels through the FIFO: when that data is read, BUFOVF and INTFLAG.ERROR set with RXC and RxDATA reads zero.

A slave (MODE = 0x2) with CTRLA.FORM = 0x2 checks the first character of each transaction against the address logic. On a match RXC sets, MISO is enabled and the transaction proceeds; otherwise the whole transaction is ignored. A match can wake the device from sleep. In 9-bit frames only the lower 8 bits are compared with ADDR.

A slave first sends what is already in its shift register: the reset value or the last character of the previous transaction. With CTRLB.PLOADEN = 1 one character written to DATA while the synchronized SS is high is preloaded into the shift register, avoiding a dummy first character; a further character written before SS falls waits in DATA. Enough time must pass between SS falling and the first SCK sampling edge to cover synchronization of SS to the system domain plus MISO set-up to SCK.

With MSSEN = 0 a master can select several parallel slaves by one GPIO SS line each, the selected slave alone driving the shared tri-state MISO. Slaves may instead be chained in series on one common SS (hardware or software driven), the master shifting n characters for n slaves.
Setting CTRLA.DIPO and CTRLA.DOPO to the same data pad loops transmit to receive through the pad, so the signal also appears on the pin.

With CTRLB.MSSEN = 1 a master drives one SS low at least one baud cycle before a transmission and keeps it low at least one baud cycle after; between back-to-back frames SS goes high for at least one baud cycle. Each of these intervals is 1 to 2 baud cycles, depending on the transfer mode. With MSSEN = 0 software drives SS through GPIO.
In slave mode with CTRLB.SSDE = 1 a falling edge on SS sets INTFLAG.SSL and can wake the device.

DMA: RX is requested while the receive FIFO holds data and cleared by reading DATA; TX is requested while TX DATA is empty and cleared by writing DATA. Interrupts: Error, Slave Select Low, Receive Complete, Transmit Complete and Data Register Empty, on one shared line, each with a flag in INTFLAG enabled by INTENSET and disabled by INTENCLR. No events.

As master the generic clock keeps running in idle; with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1 GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE also runs in standby, and with RUNSTDBY = 0 it stops when the current transaction ends; any interrupt wakes the device. As slave, RUNSTDBY = 1 lets Receive Complete wake the device; with RUNSTDBY = 0 all reception is dropped, the current transaction included.

Writes to CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE and CTRLB.RXEN are synchronized; SYNCBUSY.SWRST, SYNCBUSY.ENABLE and SYNCBUSY.CTRLB are set while each is in progress (CTRLB.RXEN has its own behaviour, given with CTRLB). A synchronized access while its SYNCBUSY bit is set gives a peripheral bus error.

I2C is a SERCOM mode, master or slave, with DMA. It is compatible with Philips I2C, SMBus and PMBus and supports 100kHz, 400kHz, 1MHz and 3.4MHz at low system clock frequencies. Outputs are slew-rate limited and inputs filtered. A slave works in every sleep mode, wakes on address match, and matches 7-bit and 10-bit addresses in hardware: a unique address and/or the 7-bit general call, an address range, or two unique addresses (usable with DMA). The master uses the baud-rate generator, the slave the address match logic.

The I2C keeps running in any sleep mode in which its clock runs and its interrupts wake the device. CLK_SERCOMx_APB is on at reset and switched in the PM. GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE clocks a master; GCLK_SERCOM_SLOW is needed only for some functions (the SMBus time-outs); both are set up in GCLK first and are asynchronous to the bus clock. It has DMA requests and an interrupt line, no events. The PAC can protect every writable register except INTFLAG, STATUS, ADDR and DATA; protection never applies to an external debugger. DBGCTRL can halt it while the CPU is halted.

SDA carries packets and SCL the clock. A transaction starts with a start condition and a 7-bit address plus a direction bit from the master; the addressed slave acknowledges and data packets follow, each 8 data bits and one acknowledge bit. After a NACK from either side the master either sends a stop condition or a repeated start to go on.

CTRLA (but ENABLE and SWRST), CTRLB (but ACKACT and CMD), BAUD, and ADDR in slave operation are writable only while the interface is disabled; writes while enabled or enabling are dropped, writes while disabling land once it is off. Setup: CTRLA.MODE = 0x4 or 0x5; optionally CTRLA.LOWTOUT for the SCL low time-out; for a master CTRLA.INACTOUT for the inactive bus time-out; CTRLA.SDAHOLD for SDA hold time; CTRLB.SMEN for smart mode; for a slave CTRLB.AMODE and the addresses in ADDR.ADDR and ADDR.ADDRMASK; for a master BAUD. CTRLA.ENABLE enables; CTRLA.SWRST resets all but DBGCTRL and disables.

Start and stop detectors and a bit counter watch the bus in every sleep mode; STATUS.BUSSTATE gives the state: UNKNOWN (0b00), IDLE (0b01), OWNER (0b10), BUSY (0b11). The state machine runs while the master is enabled and starts UNKNOWN. It goes to IDLE when software writes BUSSTATE, when a stop is seen, or on an inactive bus time-out, and never returns to UNKNOWN. From IDLE a start by another master gives BUSY until a stop (or a time-out). Writing ADDR.ADDR while IDLE issues a start and gives OWNER; a stop command returns to IDLE; a collision while OWNER loses arbitration and gives BUSY until a stop. A repeated start changes the state only if arbitration is lost during it.

In Standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus the BAUD register sets SCL low and high times and the bus sets rise and fall; the fall time counts inside TLOW (wired-AND bus) and the rise time sits between TLOW and THIGH until a high is detected. TLOW, TSU;STO, TBUF, THD;STA and TSU;STA are timed from BAUD.BAUDLOW when it is non-zero, otherwise from BAUD.BAUD; THIGH from BAUD.BAUD. TRISE depends on the bus impedance and TFALL on the bus impedance and how much current the open-drain output may sink, usually counted as zero. In high-speed mode there is no SCL synchronization: SCL comes from the GCLK frequency and HSBAUD/HSBAUDLOW.

The master is byte-oriented and interrupt-driven, handling most events itself; smart mode (CTRLA.SMEN) cuts driver code. With CTRLA.SCLSM = 0 the master holds SCL low ahead of or following the ACK bit; with SCLSM = 1 interrupts come only after the acknowledge, for when DATA need not be checked before acknowledging. High-speed mode needs SCLSM = 1.

A transaction begins when ADDR.ADDR is written with the slave's address plus the direction bit; the master waits for an idle bus, sends a start and the address. Then: (1) arbitration lost or bus error: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.ARBLOST set (with STATUS.BUSERR for a bus error), SDA output is disabled and SCL released, and the master stays off the bus until it is idle; flags clear on the next ADDR.ADDR write. (2) No ACK: MB and STATUS.RXNACK set with the clock held; next a stop (recommended) or a repeated start. Under SMBus a slave must ACK its address, so silence means it is absent. (3) Write, ACK: MB sets, RXNACK clears, clock held; next write DATA.DATA, write a new address (repeated start inserted) or stop. (4) Read, ACK: the first byte is received, INTFLAG.SB sets, RXNACK clears, clock held; next acknowledge and read on (automatic on reading DATA.DATA in smart mode), a new address, or stop, the ACK or NACK being sent per CTRLB.ACKACT. STATUS.RXNACK always holds the last acknowledge received.

After a write address is acknowledged, writing DATA.DATA sends a byte while the master watches for collisions; a collision sets STATUS.ARBLOST, success clears RXNACK on the slave's ACK, and MB sets either way. ARBLOST is best tested first in the MB handler, address and data arbitration being handled alike. RXNACK is checked after each byte; the master may not send more after a NACK. Receiving with SCLSM = 0: when SB sets one byte is in and the master must send ACK or NACK; arbitration can be lost while sending NACK, signalled by MB instead of SB. With SCLSM = 1: when SB sets the byte is in and ACKACT already sent; set ACKACT for the next bit, read DATA and issue a command if not in smart mode.

A master code 0000 1nnn is sent in full-speed mode (ADDR with ADDR.HS = 0) and is NACKed; arbitration happens only in this phase. On the master write interrupt the slave address is written with ADDR.HS = 1, giving a repeated start and the address in high-speed mode, which lasts until a stop. Each repeated start needs ADDR.HS = 1 again with the new address. High-speed mode needs CTRLA.SPEED = 0b10 and SCLSM = 1.

With ADDR.TENBITEN = 1 a write to ADDR sends the two address bytes (11110 addr[9:8] W, then addr[7:0]); the transaction always starts with the read/write bit ADDR.ADDR[0] = 0. A NACK after the first byte raises the write interrupt with NACK set; otherwise the write interrupt comes after the second byte. A read follows the 10-bit address with a repeated start and 11110 addr[9:8] 1: write ADDR.ADDR[10:1] with TENBITEN = 1 and bit 0 = 0; on the write interrupt write ADDR[7:0] = 11110 addr[9:8] 1 with TENBITEN = 0; then transfer data.

The slave is byte-oriented and interrupt-driven with smart mode (CTRLA.SMEN). With SCLSM = 0 the slave holds SCL low ahead of or following the ACK bit; with SCLSM = 1 interrupts come only after the acknowledge: on a master read the address and data interrupts arrive together after the address ACK, on a master write the first data interrupt follows the first byte and its ACK. High-speed mode needs SCLSM = 1.

After a start the address is checked; a mismatch is ignored until the next start. A match sets INTFLAG.AMATCH and SCL is held low until AMATCH is cleared, so software has unlimited time to answer (with SCLSM = 1 the ACKACT response is sent automatically first). STATUS.DIR gives the direction, updated only on a valid address. STATUS.COLL set means the last packet to this slave collided: collisions release SDA and SCL silently, following the SMBus Address Resolution Protocol. On a read (DIR = 1) an ACK sets INTFLAG.DRDY to ask for data; on a write (DIR = 0) the slave waits for data, a repeated start or a stop; after a NACK it waits for a new start. CTRLB.CMD = 3 serves both directions; writing one to AMATCH also sends ACK or NACK per CTRLB.ACKACT.

INTFLAG.DRDY sets when a byte is received or sent. Received: SCL is held low for software, and the slave acknowledges per CTRLB.ACKACT. Sent: after a NACK the slave releases SDA and expects a stop or repeated start. A stop sets INTFLAG.PREC and the slave goes idle. With CTRLA.SPEED = 0x2 and SCLSM = 1 the slave switches to high-speed on a start, master code and NACK, sets STATUS.HS, and stays there until a stop.

With ADDR.TENBITEN = 1 the two address bytes after a start are checked; the first is always acknowledged and the second raises the address interrupt. A write continues with data bytes; a read continues with a repeated start and 11110 ADDR[9:8] 1, which raises a second address interrupt with DIR set, the slave remembering it was addressed.

With CTRLB.GCMD = 1 and 7-bit addressing, a stop raises the stop interrupt if this slave was addressed since the last stop. Group commands reach several devices in one transmission ended by one stop, at which every addressed slave acts on its command.

Three hardware SCL low time-outs, timed by GCLK_SERCOM_SLOW running from a 32kHz oscillator: TTIMEOUT, one SCL low period of 25-35 ms (CTRLA.LOWTOUTEN); TLOW:SEXT, cumulative slave clock extension of 25 ms from start to stop in one message (CTRLA.SEXTTOEN); TLOW:MEXT, cumulative master clock extension of 10 ms inside a single byte, measured from start, or from an ACK, to the next ACK or stop (CTRLA.MEXTTOEN). An SMBus-compatible SDA hold time is available.

operation.topic: I2C smart mode, 4-wire mode and quick command
operation.text: Smart mode makes a read of DATA.DATA send ACK or NACK by CTRLB.ACKACT. CTRLA.PINOUT selects 4-wire mode, bypassing the internal I2C tri-state drivers; joining an I2C bus then takes an outside tri-state driver that meets the I2C spec. CTRLB.QCEN enables quick command: the flag sets right after the slave acknowledges the address, and software then issues a stop or repeated start through CTRLB.CMD or ADDR.ADDR.

DMA needs smart mode (CTRLB.SMEN). Slave: after the address match interrupt is served, data moves by DMA; RX is requested when master write data arrives (cleared by reading DATA), TX when a master read needs data (cleared by writing DATA). Master: write ADDR.ADDR with ADDR.LEN (0 to 255 bytes) and ADDR.LENEN = 1; DMA moves LEN bytes, then a NACK (on reads) and a stop follow automatically. A NACK before LEN bytes on a master write gives an automatic stop and STATUS.LENERR with INTFLAG.ERROR. RX is requested when master read data arrives, TX when a master write needs data.

Slave sources: Error, Data Ready, Address Match, Stop Received. Master sources: Error, Slave on Bus, Master on Bus. One shared line; each flag in INTFLAG is enabled by INTENSET and disabled by INTENCLR. No events.

As master GCLK_SERCOMx_CORE runs in idle, and in standby too with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1; with RUNSTDBY = 0 it stops when the current transaction ends; any interrupt wakes the device. As slave, RUNSTDBY = 1 lets Address Match wake the device; with RUNSTDBY = 0 all reception is dropped.

Synchronized writes: CTRLA.SWRST (SYNCBUSY.SWRST), CTRLA.ENABLE (SYNCBUSY.ENABLE), and STATUS.BUSSTATE, ADDR.ADDR in master operation and DATA in master operation (SYNCBUSY.SYSOP). A synchronized access while its SYNCBUSY bit is set gives a peripheral bus error.

The TC is built from a counter, its prescaler, compare/capture channels and their control. It counts clock pulses or events, can time-stamp input events to capture frequency and pulse width, and generates waveforms (frequency, single-slope PWM). It is 8, 16 or 32 bits wide, has one input event, interrupts and output events on overflow/underflow and on compare match or capture, an internal prescaler, and can use and trigger DMA.

The TC runs in any sleep mode in which its clock runs; its interrupts wake the device and its events act without waking it. CLK_TCx_APB is switched in the PM. TC instances work in even/odd pairs counted from TC1; both members of a pair share one generic clock GCLK_TCx, so the two cannot take different clocks. GCLK_TCx is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some accesses are synchronized. Events are routed through EVSYS. The TC halts when the CPU is halted by a debugger unless DBGCTRL keeps it running.
The PAC can protect every writable register except INTFLAG, STATUS, READREQ, COUNT, PER and CCx. Protection is lifted while the CPU is halted in debug and never applies to an external debugger.

The counter counts events from the Event System or GCLK_TCx pulses through the prescaler. Its value goes to the compare/capture channels, compared with set values or captured on an event. The width (8, 16 or 32 bits) and the clock set range and resolution. It counts up or down; by default it counts up continuously, wrapping to zero after the top value. Compare channels toggle output pins on match for frequency and PWM generation; capture records period and pulse width.

CTRLA (but RUNSTDBY, ENABLE and SWRST) and EVCTRL.EVACT are writable only while the TC is disabled; enable-protected CTRLA bits may be written together with ENABLE = 1 but not with ENABLE = 0. Setup: enable CLK_TCx_APB; CTRLA.MODE for 8, 16 (default) or 32 bits; CTRLA.WAVEGEN; CTRLA.PRESCALER if the clock is divided, and then CTRLA.PRESYNC; CTRLBSET.ONESHOT for one-shot; CTRLBSET.DIR to count down; CTRLC.CPTEN for capture channels; CTRLC.INVEN to invert outputs. CTRLA.ENABLE enables; CTRLA.SWRST resets all but DBGCTRL and disables the TC; disable the TC before resetting it, or behaviour is undefined.

GCLK_TC feeds a prescaler giving divisions from 1 to 1/1024 (GCLK_TC / 1, 2, 4, 8, 64, 256, 1024); it counts to the selected value and toggles its output. Above 1, CTRLA.PRESYNC chooses whether on overflow or underflow the prescaler restarts from zero or keeps counting, and whether the counter wraps on the next GCLK_TC pulse or the next prescaled pulse (CLK_TC_CNT). Counted events bypass the prescaler.

CTRLA.MODE: COUNT8 has its own period register PER, used as top for waveform generation; COUNT16, the default, has no period register; COUNT32 pairs two 16-bit TCs, the even one master and the odd one slave (STATUS.SLAVE set). The slave's registers do not show the 32-bit counter, writes to them have no effect on it, and normal access to the slave's COUNT and CCx is not allowed.

Counting up, the counter wraps to zero the clock after reaching top; counting down, it wraps to top after zero; in one-shot it stops after a wrap. CTRLBSET.DIR counts down and CTRLBCLR.DIR counts up. Reaching top or zero sets INTFLAG.OVF, and with EVCTRL.OVFEO = 1 gives an event. COUNT may be read or written; it starts at zero unless written or left at top by a stop while counting down. The stop command (CTRLBSET.CMD) holds the count, clears every waveform, stops the counter and sets STATUS.STOP.

operation.topic: TC retrigger, count and start actions
operation.text: Retrigger, by CTRLBSET.CMD or as an EVCTRL.EVACT event action, wraps a running counter to top or zero by direction and restarts a stopped one from COUNT. With a retrigger or start event action configured, enabling the TC does not start counting: it starts at the next event (or software retrigger); a retrigger action restarts it on every later event, while a start action ignores events once running. The count event action steps the counter up or down per event by CTRLBSET.DIR.

In compare operation the counter is compared with every CCx without pause. To put a waveform on a pin: pick a waveform mode, optionally invert it with CTRLC.INVx, and enable the pin multiplexer in PORT. A match sets INTFLAG.MCx on the next rising edge of CLK_TC_CNT, with an interrupt or event if INTENSET.MCx or EVCTRL.MCEOx is set. CTRLA.WAVEGEN gives Normal frequency (NFRQ), Match frequency (MFRQ), Normal PWM (NPWM) and Match PWM (MPWM). In NFRQ and NPWM the top is PER in 8-bit mode and the counter maximum in 16- and 32-bit modes.

NFRQ: WO[x] toggles and the channel flag sets on each match of CCx. MFRQ: CC0 is top and WO[0] toggles on each overflow or underflow. PWM: CCx sets duty; counting up, WO[x] sets at start or at top match and clears at the CCx match; counting down, it clears at start or top match and sets at the CCx match. In MPWM CC0 is top and WO[0] gives a negative pulse on each overflow or underflow.

The top may change while counting. Counting down, a new top written near zero may be missed through synchronization delay and the old top reloaded, costing one extra cycle. Counting up, a new top below the current count is missed and the counter runs to its maximum before wrapping.

Capture needs EVCTRL.TCEI = 1 and the channels enabled in CTRLC.CPTENx. Event capture records any EVSYS event; all channels share one event line, so only one channel should capture at a time. A capture arriving while the capture flag is still set has nowhere to go and sets INTFLAG.ERR.

EVACT = PPW captures the period into CC0 and the pulse width into CC1; PWP captures pulse width into CC0 and period into CC1. The TC captures on both edges and restarts the counter on one, the falling edge if EVCTRL.TCINV = 1. The captured event must be asynchronous. Writing CTRLC.CPTEN = 0x3 captures both; if only one figure is needed the other channel is free. Capture overflow sets INTFLAG.ERR.

CTRLBSET.ONESHOT enables and CTRLBCLR.ONESHOT disables one-shot: the counter stops at the next overflow or underflow, STATUS.STOP sets and the waveform outputs go to zero. A retrigger command, retrigger event or start event restarts it and clears STATUS.STOP.

OVF is requested on overflow or underflow and clears the next clock. MCx is requested on each match of a compare channel (cleared the next clock) or while a capture channel holds data (cleared when CCx is read). With the OVF request a new PER or CCx lands after the update, DMA and synchronization delays, so a match is missed if COUNT has already passed it. With the MCx request, a CCx below the count (counting down) or above it (counting up) can match again before overflow, starting the next transfer, so the earlier value never reaches WO[x].

Interrupts: OVF, compare or capture per channel, ERR (capture overflow) and SYNCRDY, on one shared line, each flag in INTFLAG enabled by INTENSET and disabled by INTENCLR. Output events OVF and MC are enabled in EVCTRL (MCEO). EVCTRL.EVACT selects one input action: start, retrigger, increment or decrement, capture event, capture period or capture pulse width; EVCTRL.TCEI enables the input event.
The TC can run in any sleep mode; in standby only with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1. It wakes the device by interrupt from any sleep mode or acts through the Event System.

Synchronized accesses set STATUS.SYNCBUSY until done; INTFLAG.SYNCRDY can signal the end. Another synchronized access while SYNCBUSY is set stalls the bus (and the CPU, with interrupts pending). Synchronized on write: CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, CTRLC, COUNT, PERIOD and CCx. Synchronized on read: CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, CTRLC, COUNT, PERIOD and CCx.

The TCC is a timer/counter for control applications: counter, prescaler, compare/capture channels and control logic, counting clock pulses or events, time-stamping input events for frequency and pulse-width capture, and generating frequency and PWM waveforms. Its waveform extensions serve motor control, ballast, LED, H-bridge and power converter work: low- and high-side outputs with dead time, a synchronized bit pattern across outputs, and fault handling that disables or shuts down external drivers deterministically. Instances differ in channels, outputs, width and extensions.

Up to four compare/capture channels with double-buffered period and compare/capture and circular buffers on period and compare registers. Waveforms: frequency, single-slope PWM, dual-slope PWM with half-cycle reload. Capture of events, frequency and pulse width. Extensions: configurable spread of channel outputs over pins, low- and high-side outputs with programmable dead time, swap and pattern generation (both double buffered), dithering. Faults: two recoverable and two non-recoverable sources, with the debugger able to act as a non-recoverable fault. Events: two counter inputs and one input per channel; Count, Retrigger and Overflow outputs and a match/capture output per channel. Interrupts on overflow and retrigger, match/capture and fault. DMA use and triggering.

The TCC runs in any sleep mode in which its clock runs; its interrupts wake the device and its events act without waking it. CLK_TCCx_APB is switched in the PM; GCLK_TCCx must be set up in GCLK and is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some writes are synchronized. Events go through EVSYS. The TCC halts when the CPU is halted by a debugger unless DBGCTRL keeps it running. The PAC can protect every writable register except INTFLAG, STATUS, PER/PERB, CCx/CCBx, WAVE/WAVEB and PATT/PATTB; protection never applies to an external debugger.

COUNT, PER/PERB and CCx/CCBx are 16 or 24 bits by instance; each buffer has a buffer valid (BV) flag. The counter is compared with TOP and zero, and with each CCx to raise interrupts, DMA requests or events and to shape waveforms. The counter runs from the prescaled GCLK_TCCx or from events, which also feed capture. A channel is a compare channel or a capture channel by use; 'timer' means an internal clock and 'counter' an external one.

operation.topic: TCC recoverable and non-recoverable faults, outline
operation.text: Recoverable faults act on the channel outputs from events: restart or halt the period, shorten the active time, or disable the output while the fault lasts, as for current regulation or zero-crossing and demagnetization retrigger. They share the MCE0 and MCE1 event inputs, use only asynchronous events, and can be filtered and blanked against pin glitches. Non-recoverable faults force the outputs to a preset safe level for instant shutdown of high current or voltage drives; they share the TCE0 and TCE1 inputs and, unfiltered, act asynchronously even with no clock.

Some instances carry the output matrix (OTMX), which routes waveform outputs to pins in several layouts; dead-time insertion (DTI), which splits the four lower OTMX outputs into a non-inverted low side and an inverted high side with optional dead time between them; SWAP, which exchanges the low- and high-side pins, for fast-decay motor control; and the pattern generator, which drives outputs to fixed levels on update, as for stepper and full-bridge control.

CTRLA (but RUNSTDBY, ENABLE and SWRST), FCTRLA, FCTRLB, WEXCTRL, DRVCTRL and EVCTRL are writable only while the TCC is disabled; enable-protected CTRLA bits may be written with ENABLE = 1 but not with ENABLE = 0. First enable CLK_TCCx_APB, and set CTRLA.CAPTEN for capture channels. Before or after enabling: CTRLA.PRESCALER, CTRLA.PRESCSYNC, CTRLBSET.DIR for counting down, WAVE.WAVEGEN, WAVE.POL, and DRVCTRL.INVEN to invert outputs. CTRLA.ENABLE enables; CTRLA.SWRST resets all but DBGCTRL and disables the TCC; disable it before resetting, or behaviour is undefined.

GCLK_TCCx feeds a prescaler giving divisions from 1 to 1/1024 (GCLK_TCC / 1, 2, 4, 8, 64, 256, 1024). Above 1, CTRLA.PRESYNC chooses whether on an external retrigger the prescaler restarts from zero or keeps counting, and whether the counter wraps on the next GCLK_TCC pulse or the next prescaled pulse (CLK_TCC_CNT). Counted events bypass the prescaler.

Each CLK_TCC_CNT cycle the counter clears, reloads, increments or decrements; a clear or reload ends a cycle. Counting up it clears to zero the clock after TOP; counting down it reloads PER after zero. Reaching TOP or zero sets INTFLAG.OVF, for an interrupt, DMA request or event; with CTRLBSET.ONESHOT it also stops. CTRLBCLR.DIR counts up and CTRLBSET.DIR down. COUNT may be written while running, taking priority over count, clear and reload, and direction may change at any time; settings land after synchronization. Normal operation is needed when the counter is the time base for capture.

Stop (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x2) holds the count, sets waveforms to the DRVCTRL.NREx/NRVx state and sets STATUS.STOP. Pause (EVCTRL.EVACT1 = 0x3) holds the count and waveform states until a start event (EVCTRL.EVACT0 = 0x3). Retrigger (CTRLBSET.CMD = 0x1, or EVCTRL.EVACTn = 0x1) reloads or clears a running counter by direction, sets INTFLAG.TRG, and gives an event if EVCTRL.TRGEO = 1; a stopped counter resumes from COUNT. With a retrigger event action, enabling does not start the counter: it starts on the next event and restarts on each later one.

Start (EVACT0 = 0x3) starts a stopped counter and is ignored while counting; with it configured, enabling does not start the counter, which starts on the next event (or software retrigger) and does not restart on later ones. Count (EVACT0 = 0x5) steps the counter per event by direction. Direction (EVACT1 = 0x2) sets the direction from the event level, overriding CTRLBSET/CTRLBCLR.DIR, and needs an asynchronous event path. Increment (EVACT0 = 0x4) counts up on each TCE0 event and decrement (EVACT1 = 0x4) counts down on each TCE1 event, whatever the direction. Non-recoverable fault (EVACTn = 0x7) stops the counter and overrides the outputs by DRVCTRL.NREx/NRVx; TCE0 and TCE1 must be asynchronous. With the event action off (EVACTn = 0x0) enabling starts the counter.

Channels are compare channels by default. The counter is compared with every CCx; CCBx double-buffers CCx, updating it at the UPDATE condition so that pulses are never odd-length or asymmetric and outputs are glitch-free. For a pin waveform: choose WAVE.WAVEGEN, optionally invert with DRVCTRL.INVENx, and enable PORTMUX. A match sets INTFLAG.MCx on the next rising edge of CLK_TCC_COUNT, with an interrupt (INTENSET.MCx), an event (EVCTRL.MCEOx), both, and a DMA request. Modes: NFRQ, MFRQ, NPWM, DSTOP, DSBOTTOM, DSBOTH and DSCRITICAL. MFRQ takes TOP from CC0, every other mode from PER. Dual-slope modes update at zero; the others update on wraparound (overflow, underflow or retrigger).
NFRQ: PER sets the period and WO[x] toggles on each COUNT = CCx match, setting the channel flag. MFRQ: CC0 sets the period and WO[0] toggles on each update.

PER sets the period and CCx the duty cycle. Counting up, WO[x] sets at start or the TOP match and clears at the CCx match; counting down, it clears at start or the TOP match and sets at the CCx match.

The counter runs from zero to PER and back; PER sets the period and CCx the duty cycle. The output sets on the match counting up and clears on the match counting down. The interrupt or event comes at TOP, zero or both by mode; DSBOTH adds a second update at TOP. The highest frequency is lower than in single-slope PWM. In DSTOP, DSBOTTOM and DSBOTH with TOP below MAX/2, the MSB of CCx chooses the slope where its match raises the interrupt or event: the rising slope for 0, the falling one for 1.
DSCRITICAL makes non-aligned centred pulses: PER sets the period, CCx sets the output edge while counting up and CC(x + CC_NUM/2) the edge while counting down.
WAVE.POLx applies in every waveform mode; in single- and dual-slope PWM it flips, per channel, whether the pulse aligns to the start or end of the cycle.

PATT, WAVE, PER and CCx are double buffered by PATTB, WAVEB, PERB and CCBx, with valid bits PATTBV, WAVEBV, PERBV and CCBVx in STATUS. With buffering on (CTRLBCLR.LUPD written) and PER and CCx in compare use, a valid bit sets when its buffer is written and clears at update. Writing CTRLBSET.LUPD turns buffering off so registers can be written directly. In NFRQ, MFRQ or down-counting PWM, PER is written together with PERB when LUPD is zero, or as soon as it becomes zero.

PER or PERB takes a new period. Unbuffered, a new PER acts after the synchronization delay; counting up in any mode, a new TOP below the current count is missed and the counter wraps through MAX. Buffered, PERB may be written at any time and PER loads at the update, avoiding wraparound and odd waveforms.

Capture needs EVCTRL.MCEIx and CTRLA.CPTENx. Each channel has its own event line, so several captures can run at once. CCBx and CCx form a two-deep queue: once CCx has been read, or holds nothing, CCBx moves into it and its valid flag sets the channel flag, with the optional interrupt, event or DMA request. A capture with MCx and the buffer valid flag both set has nowhere to go and sets INTFLAG.ERR.

EVACT1 = PPW captures period into CC0 and pulse width into CC1; PWP the reverse. Capture happens on both edges, and EVCTRL.TCEINV1 picks the edge that restarts the counter. The captured event must be asynchronous. CTRLA.CPTENx enables CC0 and CC1; if only one figure is needed the other channel is free. Overflow sets INTFLAG.ERR. In dual-slope PWM with TOP below MAX/2, the CCx MSB records the direction at capture: 0 rising, 1 falling.

With CTRLBSET.ONESHOT (cleared by CTRLBCLR.ONESHOT) the counter stops at the next overflow or underflow, STATUS.STOP sets and outputs take the DRVCTRL.NREx/NRVx values. A retrigger command, retrigger event or start event restarts it and clears STATUS.STOP.
PER and CC0 to CC3 can run as circular buffers: at each update PER or CCx is copied into its buffer register. Circular buffers serve RAMP2, RAMP2A and DSBOTH.

Dithering adds extra clock cycles over a frame of 16, 32 or 64 PWM cycles to refine the average pulse width or period, one cycle at a time on some compare matches, spread by a blue-noise sequence that limits flicker. CTRLA.RESOLUTION: DITH4 every 16 frames, DITH5 every 32, DITH6 every 64. In COUNT, PER and CCx the low DITHERCY field holds the extra cycles per frame and the upper bits hold the value itself. A cycle gets an extra clock when ((MASK AND cycle × DITHERCY) + DITHERCY) > MASK, with MASK = 0x0F, 0x1F or 0x3F for DITH4, DITH5 and DITH6.

All ramps use single-slope PWM. RAMP1 is the default single-slope PWM. RAMP2 interleaves two timer cycles, A and B, for PFC, half-bridge and push-pull SMPS: odd channel outputs are off in cycle A and even ones in cycle B; the ramp index changes at each update and CTRLBSET.IDXCMD can set it. In standard RAMP2, PER sets both periods, different per ramp with the circular buffer (CIPEREN); a two-channel TCC gives two outputs, or one output and a capture channel. In RAMP2A, CC0 drives both WO[0] and WO[1] with its circular buffer enabled, both with the same polarity, leaving channel 1 for capture.

Fault A and Fault B act on CC0 and CC1, clamping their outputs inactive while the fault lasts or from the first valid fault to the end of the cycle; they can also restart or halt the counter. Their inputs are the first two channel input events (MC0, MC1) on asynchronous EVSYS channels. Filters, usable alone or together: input filtering (asynchronous by default, acting even in power modes with no clock; FCTRLn.FILTERVAL delays the event that many clocks and drops shorter events); blanking (FCTRLn.BLANK picks the output edge, FCTRLn.BLANKVAL the clocks to ignore the input after it, at most 256 clocks); qualification (FCTRLn.QUAL ignores the input while the channel output is inactive).

Actions can combine. Keep (FCTRLn.KEEP): the output is clamped to zero while the fault lasts and released at the start of the first cycle after it ends. Restart (FCTRLn.RESTART): the cycle stops and a new one begins, outputs clamped inactive while the fault lasts; in RAMP2 the cycle index advances, and Fault A acts only in cycle A, Fault B only in cycle B. Hardware halt (FCTRLn.HALT = HW): the counter halts and the cycle stretches while the fault lasts, channel 0 output inactive, resuming when it clears, or restarting then if restart is also on. Software halt (HALT = SWHALT): as hardware halt, but restarting also needs the STATUS.FAULTn bit cleared.

FCTRLn.CAPTURE captures the count at the fault: CAPT, a normal capture with MCx set on every capture; CAPTMIN and CAPTMAX, capturing only a new minimum or maximum so CCx holds the extreme, with MCx on each new capture; LOCMIN and LOCMAX, capturing every time but flagging only a value lower or higher than the last; DERIV0, the OR of LOCMIN and LOCMAX. In LOCMIN, LOCMAX and DERIV0 CCx follows the count at each fault.

A non-recoverable fault forces every compare output to the level set in DRVCTRL.NRE and DRVCTRL.NRV. Inputs EV0 and EV1 are enabled through EVCTRL.EVACT0 and EVCTRL.EVACT1. DRVCTRL.FILTERVALn adds a digital filter against glitches, making detection synchronous and delaying the action by the filter value in clocks.

After the recoverable fault stage, DTI and SWAP work on pin pairs: slice x acts on WO[x] and WO[WO_NUM/2 + x]. Output matrix layouts (WEXCTRL.OTMX): 0x0, the default, puts channel n on OTMX[n], repeating from OTMX[CC_NUM] when there are more outputs than channels; 0x1 repeats modulo half the channels, so two channels can drive the four switches of a full bridge, with pattern generation overriding outputs for all-quadrant control; 0x2 puts CC0 on every pin, for a stepper with pattern generation; 0x3 puts CC0 on the first output and CC1 on all others, with pattern generation and faults running as many as seven LED strings behind a boost converter.

Dead time is an interval with the low side (non-inverted) and the high side (inverted) both forced low, so they never switch together. Four DTI generators serve channels 0 to 3 and share a single dead-time register independent of the side settings. An 8-bit counter counts down one per peripheral clock to zero, holding both outputs off while non-zero; a rising edge of the OTMX output reloads it from DTLS and a falling edge from DTHS.

The pattern generator puts a synchronized bit pattern on its pins, for BLDC commutation, stepper and full-bridge control. PATT.PGE enables override per output and PATT.PGV gives the level; PGEB and PGVB buffer them and load at UPDATE, or PATT may be written directly when synchronization is not needed.

DMA: OVF is requested on update (overflow, underflow or retrigger); MCx on each match of a compare channel, or while a capture channel holds data, cleared by reading CCx. Interrupts: OVF, TRG, CNT, ERR, DFS (debug fault state), FAULTn (recoverable), FAULTx (non-recoverable) and MCx, on one shared line, flags in INTFLAG enabled by INTENSET and disabled by INTENCLR. Output events OVF, TRG, CNT and MCx are enabled by EVCTRL.xxEO. Channel input events capture or raise a recoverable fault. EV1: retrigger, direction, stop, decrement, period and pulse-width capture, non-recoverable fault. EV0: retrigger, count by direction, start (later events do not restart it), increment regardless of direction, count while an asynchronous event is active, non-recoverable fault. EVCTRL.MCEIx and TCEIx enable inputs; an enabled action applies to every event connected.
The TCC can run in any sleep mode; in standby only with CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1. It wakes the device by interrupt from any sleep mode or acts through the event system.

A synchronized access sets its SYNCBUSY bit until done; an access while that bit is set triggers a hardware interrupt. Synchronized on write: CTRLA.SWRST and CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLBCLR, CTRLBSET, STATUS, PATT, PATTB, WAVE, WAVEB, COUNT, PER, PERB, CCx and CCBx.

A 12-bit ADC converting at up to 350ksps (350,000 samples per second), with 8-, 10- or 12-bit results (fewer bits convert faster). Inputs are single-ended or differential, up to 32 analog inputs (25 positive and 10 negative, internal and external), with five internal inputs: bandgap, temperature sensor, DAC, scaled core supply and scaled I/O supply. A gain stage gives 1/2x to 16x. Conversions are single, continuous or pin-scan, started by software or by an event for predictable timing. Results are signed or unsigned, left- or right-adjusted, and can move by DMA. A window monitor watches thresholds on a chosen channel. Conversion range: Vref from 1v to VDDANA - 0.6V; ADCx * GAIN from 0V to -Vref. Internal and external references with four bits of selection; hardware gain and offset compensation; averaging and oversampling with decimation up to a 16-bit result; selectable sampling time; one event input.

The ADC runs in any sleep mode in which its clock runs; its interrupts wake the device and its events act without waking it. CLK_ADC_APB is switched in the PM; GCLK_ADC must be set up in GCLK and is asynchronous to the bus clock, so some accesses are synchronized. DMA, interrupt and EVSYS connections are used once their controllers are set up. The ADC halts when the CPU is halted by a debugger unless DBGCTRL keeps it running. The PAC can protect every writable register except INTFLAG; protection is lifted while the CPU is halted in debug or its reset is extended, and never applies to an external debugger. Pins AIN0 to AIN19 and VREFA/VREFB are its analog inputs.
The rated accuracy needs BIAS_CAL and LINEARITY_CAL, written at production test into the NVM calibration row, copied by software into CALIB.

Results are 12-bit by default; 8 or 10 bits shorten conversion and oversampling with decimation reaches 16 bits. Inputs may be internal (the temperature sensor, for example) or pins, single-ended or differential. Before enabling, select and enable the GCLK_ADC source and set the reference; discard the first conversion after a reference change, and keep all other configuration stable during a conversion. CTRLA.ENABLE enables and 0 disables; CTRLA.SWRST resets all but DBGCTRL and disables the ADC, which must be disabled before reset.

The ADC samples the inputs chosen in INPUTCTRL at a rate set by GCLK_ADC and the prescaler. A conversion starts on SWTRIG.START or an automatic trigger; free-running mode starts each conversion when the last ends. Each result overwrites RESULT. With more than one channel enabled each result must be read when INTFLAG.RESRDY sets, or INTFLAG.OVERRUN flags the loss. INTENSET enables interrupts.
GCLK_ADC passes a 9-bit prescaler whose DIV4 to DIV512 output, chosen by CTRLB.PRESCALER[2:0], is CLK_ADC. CTRLB.RESSEL selects 8, 10 or 12 bits; 12 bits after reset.

Single-ended conversion suits a positive input always above the negative and gives full 12-bit positive results; its negative input goes to ground (internal GND, IOGND or a ground pin, by INPUTCTRL). Differential conversion (CTRLB.DIFFMODE) handles a positive input that may go below the negative and gives signed results. Either runs single or free-running; in free-running INTFLAG.RESRDY sets at each conversion end.

A write of SWTRIG.START or EVCTRL.STARTEI has to lead the CLK_ADC cycle that begins the conversion by one or more CLK_ADC_APB cycles. Sampling occupies the opening half of a CLK_ADC period, and SAMPCTRL.SAMPLEN extends it. Without gain, a differential conversion takes the sample half-period and then resolves MSB to LSB over the following CLK_ADC cycles; single-ended mode adds an amplify phase after sampling.

AVGCTRL.SAMPLENUM sets how many consecutive results are accumulated; beyond 16 the sum is shifted right automatically to fit the 16-bit RESULT. Averaging divides the sum of m samples by m, using the automatic shift plus AVGCTRL.ADJRES; it improves accuracy in noise at the cost of rate, and RESRDY sets when the average is ready. Accumulating or averaging two or more samples needs CTRLB.RESSEL written to one.
Adding n bits of resolution, up to 16 bits in all, takes 4^n accumulated samples shifted right by n, the shift split between the automatic shift and AVGCTRL.ADJRES.

WINCTRL.WINMODE[2:0] picks the comparison against WINLT and WINUT; INTFLAG.WINMON sets on a match. Thresholds are signed in differential mode and unsigned otherwise, and only the bits of the CTRLB.RESSEL resolution count: in 8-bit mode the lower eight, with the eighth bit taken as the sign in differential mode even if the ninth is zero.

Offset error is the transfer function's departure from the ideal line at zero input, removed by subtracting OFFSETCORR before RESULT is written. Gain error is the departure of the last step's midpoint from the ideal line after offset correction, removed by GAINCORR. Both need CTRLB.CORREN = 1. Correction adds 13 GCLK_ADC of latency to a single conversion; in free-running mode it shows only on the first conversion, the rest arriving at the set rate.

DMA: RESRDY is requested when a result (or a finished average) is ready and cleared when RESULT is read. Interrupts: RESRDY, OVERRUN, WINMON and SYNCRDY, each flag in INTFLAG enabled by INTENSET, disabled by INTENCLR and cleared by writing one; RESRDY, WINMON and SYNCRDY are asynchronous and wake the device from any sleep mode. Output events RESRDY and WINMON are enabled by EVCTRL.xxEO; input events START and FLUSH by EVCTRL.xxEI, an enabled action applying to every event connected.

With CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 0 the ADC is disabled in standby, keeping its configuration, and its analog blocks power off, so a start-up delay follows wake-up. With RUNSTDBY = 1 it keeps running, any enabled ADC interrupt wakes the CPU, and while the CPU sleeps only events trigger conversions.

Synchronized accesses set STATUS.SYNCBUSY until done; SYNCRDY can signal the end. Another synchronized access while SYNCBUSY is set stalls the bus (and the CPU, with interrupts pending). Synchronized on write: CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, CTRLB, SWTRIG, WINCTRL, INPUTCTRL, WINUT and WINLT. Synchronized on read: SWTRIG, INPUTCTRL and RESULT.

The analog comparator block holds one pair of comparators, COMP0 and COMP1, each with its own control registers. Each compares a positive and a negative input and gives a one when the positive side is higher. The positive input comes from the four shared pins AIN0 to AIN3; the negative input from those pins, ground, the bandgap, a 64-step VDDANA scaler per comparator, or the DAC. Speed against current and hysteresis on or off are selectable; outputs can go to the CMP pins, synchronous or not. Interrupts fire on rising, falling or either edge, or at the end of a comparison; events come from the outputs and from the window function. A 3- or 5-sample majority filter and single-shot operation are available.

CLK_AC_APB is gated in the Power Manager. GCLK_AC_DIG sets the comparator sampling rate; GCLK_AC_ANA keeps the input multiplexer resistance low when VDDANA is below 2.5 V. Both are asynchronous to the bus clock and must be set up in the GCLK controller first. The AC has no DMA request; it keeps working with the CPU halted in debug. All writable registers except CTRLB and INTFLAG can be PAC write-protected. Pins used as inputs must be set to analog, and an internal source (bandgap, DAC) must be enabled before it is selected. The AC runs in any sleep mode where its clock runs, and its interrupts can wake the device.

EVCTRL is written before the AC is enabled and is fixed while enabled. Each COMPCTRLx (SINGLE, HYST, SPEED, INTSEL, MUXPOS, MUXNEG, FLEN) is set before that comparator is enabled and is fixed while it runs. CTRLA.ENABLE turns the block on and COMPCTRLx.ENABLE each comparator; clearing CTRLA.ENABLE stops both without clearing their enable bits. CTRLA.SWRST resets every register except DEBUG and disables the AC.

After a comparator is enabled its output is unavailable for a start-up time, measured automatically to track temperature and supply. Below 2.5 V supply the start-up also waits for the voltage doubler, which lowers the input multiplexer resistance and switches itself with the supply level. With the supply known to stay above 2.5 V, CTRLA.LPMUX = 1 turns the doubler off, saving current and shortening start-up.

With COMPCTRLx.SINGLE = 0 the comparator runs all the time. After the first start-up STATUSA.STATEx always holds the newest result, STATUSB.READYx is set and events and interrupts follow; later comparisons need no start-up time. Edges for interrupts are found by comparing each sample with the previous one at the GCLK_AC_DIG rate. In sleep without a clock the comparator stays on and a change is detected asynchronously; the Power Manager then starts GCLK_AC_DIG long enough to post the event or interrupt, and stops it again unless the device is to wake.

With COMPCTRLx.SINGLE = 1 the comparator idles until CTRLB.STARTx is written to one, which also clears STATUSB.READYx; after the start-up time one comparison updates STATUSA, READYx sets and events and interrupts follow. Reading STATUSC starts a comparison on every single-shot comparator and holds the bus until all are ready; a comparator already busy finishes its current comparison without starting a new one. EVCTRL.COMPEIx lets an incoming event start the comparison instead, each comparator on its own event. Edge detection compares the result with the one before. In sleep an event starts GCLK_AC_DIG and the comparator, and both stop again afterwards unless the device is to wake.

COMPCTRLx.INTSEL picks the interrupt: output toggle, rising edge, falling edge, or end of comparison. End of comparison suits single-shot chains regardless of the result. Output events follow the comparator state whether or not the interrupt is enabled.

MUXPOS selects a pin for the positive input; MUXNEG selects a pin or an internal reference for the negative input. A pin used this way must have its digital input and output disabled in PORT. The multiplexers switch so as to limit crosstalk, and the selection may change only while that comparator is disabled.

WINCTRL.WENx joins the pair into a window comparator; both must use the same SINGLE setting. The signal goes to both positive inputs (the same pin) and the two negative inputs set the upper and lower limits, in either order. STATUS.WSTATEx gives the window state. WINCTRL.WINTSELx picks an interrupt on entering, leaving, going above or going below the window; window events follow the inside/outside state regardless of the interrupt. Each comparator's own output, interrupt and events keep working. In single-shot window mode either STARTx bit or either input event measures on both comparators together.
Each comparator has its own 64-level fraction of the supply as a reference, selected by MUXNEG = 5 and enabled with the comparator. SCALERx.VALUE[5:0] picks the level.

COMPCTRLx.HYST enables hysteresis per comparator to stop noise from toggling the output when the inputs are close; it works only in continuous mode. COMPCTRLx.SPEED sets the bias current, trading propagation delay against current and also changing start-up time. COMPCTRLx.FLEN selects no filter or a 3- or 5-sample majority filter, sampled at CLK_AC divided by CTRLA.PRESCALER. In continuous mode the first filtered output comes after N samples and then one per cycle. In sleep, filtering works only for single-shot measurements; it must be off for continuous measurement in sleep or events and interrupts can be wrong.

COMPCTRLx.OUT routes the comparator to its CMP pin, either raw and unsynchronized or synchronized to CLK_AC with filtering. COMPCTRLx.SWAP exchanges the two inputs and inverts the output, so the input offset can be measured or cancelled; it may change only while the comparator is disabled.

Interrupt sources are COMP0, COMP1 (per INTSEL) and WIN0 (per WINCTRL.WINTSEL), each flag in INTFLAG enabled by INTENSET, disabled by INTENCLR and cleared by writing one. Output events COMPEO0, COMPEO1 and WINEO0 are enabled in EVCTRL. Input events start a single-shot measurement, or one on both comparators in window mode, after the start-up time; with several events routed in, any of them triggers the action.

With CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 0 the pair is off in standby, keeps its settings, and needs a start-up time after wake. With RUNSTDBY = 1 it keeps running, any enabled AC interrupt wakes the CPU, and while the CPU sleeps single-shot comparisons start only from events. CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, COMPCTRLn.ENABLE and the WINCTRL register are synchronized on write; STATUS.SYNCBUSY is set during synchronization, and a further synchronized access meanwhile stalls the bus.

One 10-bit DAC channel converts up to 350 ksps. A conversion starts when DATA is written, or on an event, and the voltage appears after the conversion time. The output can drive the VOUT pin through a high-drive buffer and can feed the analog comparator and the ADC internally. DMA is supported.

CLK_DAC_APB is gated in the Power Manager; GCLK_DAC, asynchronous to the bus, clocks the converter and must be set up first. The DAC works in any sleep mode where its clock runs, keeps running with the CPU halted in debug, and has a DMA request and one interrupt line. All writable registers except INTFLAG can be PAC write-protected; protection is lifted while the CPU is halted in debug and never applies to an external debugger.

CTRLB.REFSEL is set before CTRLA.ENABLE turns the DAC on; CTRLA.SWRST resets it. CTRLB.EOEN enables the output buffer on VOUT, which drives resistive and capacitive loads; it should be on only when the pin is used. The output spans GND to the reference: INT1V (default), AVCC = VDDANA, or VREFA. CTRLB.IOEN feeds the output to the analog comparator, and can be on together with EOEN; feeding the ADC needs the output buffer on.

DATABUF and DATA form a two-stage FIFO. With EVCTRL.STARTEI set, each Start Conversion event moves DATABUF into DATA and starts a conversion; an event with DATABUF empty raises Underrun. When DATABUF empties the DAC raises the Data Buffer Empty DMA request, interrupt and (with EVCTRL.EMPTYEO) event; the request clears when DATABUF is written. DATABUF is not empty at start, so the CPU writes it before the first event. CPU access to the registers behind a DMA request can lose the request or corrupt the transfer. While the PAC protects the DAC, DATABUF cannot be written unless CTRLB.BDWP = 1.

operation.topic: DAC voltage pump and sampling period
operation.text: Below 2.5 V supply the voltage pump must run; it turns on automatically. CTRLB.VPD = 1 turns it off to save current above 2.5 V. The pump runs from GCLK_DAC, which must be at least four times the sampling rate. No flag marks the end of a conversion, so the sampling period must be at least the conversion time.

operation.topic: DAC interrupts, events, sleep and synchronization
operation.text: Interrupt sources are Data Buffer Empty, Underrun and Synchronization Ready on one shared line; INTFLAG shows which. The output event is EMPTY and the input action is START, any routed event triggering it. In idle the generic clock keeps running; in standby the output buffer holds its value if CTRLA.RUNSTDBY = 1 and is disabled otherwise. CTRLA.SWRST, CTRLA.ENABLE, DATA and DATABUF are synchronized on write and DATA on read; STATUS.SYNCBUSY marks a synchronization in progress, and the bus stalls if another synchronized access comes meanwhile.

The peripheral touch controller measures capacitive sensors whose electrodes, usually on the PCB, connect straight to I/O pins. Mutual capacitance uses one X pin (driven) and one Y pin (sensed) per line of an X-Y matrix, including ITO grids; self capacitance uses one Y pin per sensor. Both kinds can be mixed. It handles buttons, sliders, wheels and proximity, compensates parasitic capacitance with adjustable gain, recalibrates automatically, filters noise in hardware and de-synchronizes against conducted noise, and has a selectable channel-change delay. Acquisition starts on command or on an event and ends with an interrupt; scanning 10 channels every 50 ms takes about 5% of the CPU. It is used through the QTouch Library, configured with QTouch Composer.

X and Y lines connect directly to the electrodes; no external parts are needed, though a 1 kΩ series resistor on each line improves EMC. GCLK_PTC clocks the PTC, asynchronous to the system clocks; its source is chosen in the GCLK controller and has to be switched on in the Power Manager (off by default). GCLK_PTC runs from 400 kHz to 4 MHz.

Typical values are at 25 °C unless stated; minimum and maximum values hold over the whole operating temperature and voltage range unless stated. Stress beyond the absolute maximum ratings can destroy the device, and long exposure at those limits can reduce reliability; every other figure assumes the general operating conditions.

Each peripheral figure is measured by enabling the peripheral's GCLK and bus clock and the peripheral itself, putting the CPU in IDLE0, measuring, waking through the EIC (asynchronous level detection, no filter), then disabling it again; the figure is that current minus the default-state current.

operation.topic: XOSC, XOSC32 and reset pins as I/O
operation.text: Used as plain I/O, the XOSC and XOSC32 pins and the external reset pin have the normal I/O pin characteristics.

The sensor is linear, but its reading depends on INT1V, which drifts with temperature. A read-only Temperature Log row at 0x00806030, written in production test, holds the room and hot insertion temperatures, the 12-bit ADC result at each and INT1V at each. For example ROOM_TEMP_VAL_INT = 25 with ROOM_TEMP_VAL_DEC = 2 means 25.2 °C. Software interpolates a coarse temperature assuming INT1V = 1 V, interpolates INT1V at that temperature, then recomputes a fine temperature with the corrected INT1V.

Typical average PTC current at VDD = 3.3 V and a 48 MHz CPU clock, with one sample per measurement: one sensor scanned every 10 ms draws about 96 µA without frequency hopping; 50 sensors scanned every 50 ms draw about 620 µA.
Junction temperature follows TJ = TA + PD × θJA; with a heatsink the junction-to-case resistance plus the heatsink resistance replaces θJA. The first form shows whether a cooling device is needed.

In an electrically noisy setting the decoupling capacitors close to the power pins, an RC filter on RESET and a pull-up on SWCLK are essential, along with keeping noise off the supply and I/O pins and the crystal.
One supply of 1.62 V to 3.63 V feeds the device through the combined VDDIO/IN/ANA pin. Decouple it with 100 nF close to the pin plus 4.7 µF.

VREFA (PA03) and VREFB (PA04) need decoupling only when an external reference is used: 4.7 µF at the source and 100 nF at each pin. One source can feed both pins. The reference range is 1.0 V to VDDANA - 0.6 V for both ADC and DAC.

RESET works as reset after power-up and can become a GPIO through the EXTCTRL register. It has an internal pull-up, so the external 10 kΩ is optional; a 100 nF capacitor filters it, and a 330 Ω resistor in series with the reset switch limits the discharge current of that capacitor and the noise spike it would cause. Without the external reset function the circuit can be left out, and the switch is optional.
Unused pins left in their reset state already give the lowest leakage; they need no configuration.

Internal and external clock sources can be mixed, for example OSC8M for the system clock and a 32.768 kHz crystal for the RTC. An external clock goes into XIN, leaving XOUT free as GPIO. A 0.4 MHz to 30 MHz crystal goes between XIN and XOUT with 15 pF to ground on each side, kept near the device, since long traces add load and crosstalk.

The XOSC32K oscillator is tuned for 32.768 kHz watch crystals and very low current, so crystal load capacitance and ESR need care; the maximum ESR is 100 kΩ for a 12.5 pF crystal. Its internal load capacitance plus the PCB can be enough for a crystal below 12.5 pF without external capacitors; external capacitors (22 pF in the example) improve accuracy and safety factor where the crystal maker asks for them. External parasitic capacitance is usually small enough to ignore.

Programming and debugging use the Serial Wire Debug interface, supported by debuggers such as SAM-ICE, JTAGICE3 and the Xplained Pro on-board debugger. A 1 kΩ pull-up on SWCLK is needed for reliable operation. The JTAGICE3 lacks the Cortex 10-pin layout, so it uses its own 10-pin header or a squid cable.
